razor_priya: Pattern: I defaulted to medicine_cabinet_ba1 based on day 9 evidence, ignoring the rotation. Reality: At 07:00 on day 10, it was at bathroom_shelf_ba1. It rotates among shelf, sink, and medicine cabinet without a fixed daily schedule. Next time: Do not default to any single spot. Check all three bathroom spots (shelf, sink, medicine cabinet) with equal weight, prioritizing the most recent confirmed location if available, but be prepared for it to have moved to any of the other two.

glass_priya: Pattern: I incorrectly guessed kitchen_table_k1 for a late-night query, likely confusing it with mug_priya’s morning location or misremembering the item’s range. Reality: At 22:14 on day 10, it was at nightstand_b1. It moves between living room (coffee_table_l1) and bedroom (nightstand_b1). Next time: Do not check kitchen spots for glass_priya. For evening/late-night queries, check nightstand_b1 and coffee_table_l1 with equal weight. Look for specific evidence of movement between these two spots.

mug_priya: Pattern: I assumed it was in cupboard_k1 in the morning. Reality: At 07:27 on day 9, it was at kitchen_table_k1. Previous notes suggested desk_b1 for evenings, but morning location is distinct. Next time: Check kitchen_table_k1 for morning queries; do not assume cupboard_k1.

General Note: Avoid rigid location rules for glass_priya, mug_priya, and razor_priya. These items move frequently. For glass_priya, only living room and bedroom spots are valid; kitchen is incorrect. For mug_priya, kitchen_table_k1 is a common morning spot. For razor_priya, all three bathroom spots are valid. Always prioritize recent specific evidence over general patterns, but recognize that "recent" may be from a different day if the item rotates.
